_meta.title: GridWise -- Independent Adversarial Test Pack (unofficial, not organizer-issued)
_meta.purpose: A supplementary, hand-built set of 10 fresh test cases for local validation, created independently of the organizer's public sample pack to probe paraphrase robustness, boundary conditions, and failure-mode honesty that the 10 official public samples don't specifically exercise. This is NOT an official organizer artifact and is NOT the hidden judge set -- it is a team-internal QA tool.
how_to_use: POST each case's 'input' object to POST /optimize-energy, exactly like the official public sample pack.
Compare the response's directive_interpretation against 'ground_truth_directive_interpretation' (hand-derived independently from the note wording, the same way a hidden-case judge would grade it).
Replay the returned hourly_plan against the ground-truth directives and the normal GridWise energy/battery rules.

Read each case's 'rationale' before assuming a mismatch is your bug -- two cases (ADV-03, ADV-09) document known gaps found during testing as of the date below, included so a fix can be verified against a concrete repro rather than a vague description.
ADV-09 intentionally has no single correct expected schedule -- see its rationale.
known_gaps_at_time_of_writing: ADV-03: 'from X through Y' time-range wording extracts only the start hour instead of the full start-inclusive/end-exclusive range that 'until'/'to' phrasing correctly produces for the identical scenario.

ADV-09: when an extracted directive makes the LP infeasible, the service silently solves without the directive but still reports applies:true for it in directive_interpretation, instead of reflecting that the directive was not actually applied.

cases.label: All-distractor request (no real directive)

operator_notes: The vice-chancellor's office requested updated attendance sheets by Friday.
Parking permits for visiting faculty will be reissued next semester.
The library extended weekend hours starting next month.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: This note does not affect today's 24-hour energy schedule.
This note does not affect today's 24-hour energy schedule.
This note does not affect today's 24-hour energy schedule.

cases.rationale: All three notes are administrative/unrelated. Every entry must be no_op; nothing should be applied to the schedule.

cases.label: Extreme solar reduction, worded as 'almost nothing'

operator_notes: Emergency tarp covering over the solar array from 9 AM to 11 AM will cut output to almost nothing, about a 95% loss.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: Ground-truth solar_reduction directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.

cases.rationale: Tests near-total solar loss worded without a clean round percentage ('almost nothing, about a 95% loss') -> factor should be approximately 0.05.

cases.label: Reserve directive using 'through' as a range word (known LLM gap)

operator_notes: For tonight's emergency generator test we must have no less than 150 kWh sitting in the battery continuously from 7 PM through 8 PM.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: Ground-truth minimum_battery_reserve directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.

cases.rationale: KNOWN GAP: at time of writing, the deployed service interprets 'from 7 PM through 8 PM' as hours [19] only (treating 'through' as covering a single named hour) instead of [19, 20], which is what the Problem Statement's own start-inclusive/end-exclusive convention implies for that phrasing. The same battery/notes wording with 'until' or 'to' instead of 'through' correctly returns [19, 20]. The expected_output below reflects the CORRECT [19, 20] reading; a service with this gap will report a materially cheaper, non-compliant schedule instead. Also stresses a battery that starts well below the requested reserve.

cases.label: Two directives on the exact same overlapping hours

operator_notes: Battery charging must stop completely between 3 PM and 5 PM for a firmware update.
Also keep a minimum of 60 kWh in the battery at all times from 3 PM to 5 PM in case the update fails and we need backup power.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: Ground-truth no_charge_window directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.
Ground-truth minimum_battery_reserve directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.

cases.rationale: Two different directive types (no_charge_window and minimum_battery_reserve) apply to the identical hour range from two separate notes. Both must be enforced simultaneously.

cases.label: Single-hour boundary window (hour 23 only)

operator_notes: Grid purchases must not go above 60 kWh during the very last hour of the day, from 11 PM to midnight, due to a metering test.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: Ground-truth max_grid_window directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.

cases.rationale: Tests a directive confined to a single boundary hour (23) at the very edge of the 24-hour horizon, with a cap tight enough to force real battery engagement but not so tight it's infeasible.

cases.label: 24-hour clock notation instead of AM/PM

operator_notes: The battery charging circuit will be offline from 02:00 to 05:00 for scheduled maintenance.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: Ground-truth no_charge_window directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.

cases.rationale: Tests 24-hour clock notation ('02:00 to 05:00') instead of the AM/PM phrasing used in all public samples, for the same no_charge_window pattern as SAMPLE-02.

cases.label: Spelled-out numbers ('half', 'ten in the morning') instead of digits

operator_notes: Roughly half of our usual solar output will be lost to haze between ten in the morning and noon.
The campus shuttle route changes starting next week.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: Ground-truth solar_reduction directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.
This note does not affect today's 24-hour energy schedule.

cases.rationale: Tests fully spelled-out quantities and times ('roughly half', 'ten in the morning', 'noon') with no digits or percent signs anywhere in the note, plus one distractor.

cases.label: Battery starts exactly at its minimum reserve, no directive

operator_notes: No special operating conditions today; run as usual.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: This note does not affect today's 24-hour energy schedule.

cases.rationale: Battery's initial_energy_kwh equals its minimum_energy_kwh exactly (zero discharge headroom at hour 0). No operator directive applies; this purely stresses the optimizer's feasibility handling at a boundary state.

cases.label: Deliberately infeasible grid cap (stress test for the fallback path)

operator_notes: A transformer fault means we can only pull 15 kWh from the grid, at most, in each hour between 6 PM and 8 PM tonight.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: Ground-truth max_grid_window directive derived directly from the operator note's wording.

cases.rationale: DELIBERATE STRESS TEST, NOT a normal case: the requested 15 kWh/hour grid cap for hours 18-19 is mathematically infeasible given demand and the battery's max_discharge_kwh_per_hour (verified independently: even a full 55 kWh/hour discharge plus a 15 kWh grid cap cannot cover the ~205 kWh hourly demand). The Problem Statement guarantees organizer scoring scenarios are always feasible, so this exact situation should not occur in real judging -- but it is a useful test of what the service does when an LP genuinely has no solution under the extracted directive. KNOWN GAP at time of writing: the deployed service falls back to a schedule with the directive silently disabled, cost 34010.0, while STILL reporting applies:true for the directive in directive_interpretation -- i.e. it claims the directive was understood and applied when the returned schedule does not honor it at all. There is no single correct expected_output for this case; the point of including it is to check whether a service is honest about non-application when it happens, not to check a specific number.

cases.label: Distractors that mention 'solar'/'battery' words but aren't directives

operator_notes: The solar panel vendor's invoice and the battery supplier's warranty documents are both due for annual renewal paperwork next quarter.
IT is replacing laptop batteries for the admin office next week, unrelated to the campus power system.

ground_truth_directive_interpretation.explanation: This note does not affect today's 24-hour energy schedule.
This note does not affect today's 24-hour energy schedule.

cases.rationale: Both notes mention 'solar panel' / 'battery' vocabulary but describe administrative paperwork, not operating conditions. Designed to catch keyword-matching implementations that key off vocabulary rather than genuine semantic understanding; both entries must be no_op.
